To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Gaussian processes are a promising technique for learning prediction and observation models for Bayes filtering and that the resulting filters, GP-BayesFilters, are competitive with state-of-the-art techniques.

1) Gaussian process models can improve the accuracy of Bayesian filters, especially in cases where the parametric models used to represent the prediction and observation functions are inaccurate; and 2) particle filters are the most robust of the Bayesian filtering algorithms considered in this paper.
GP-BayesFilters can outperform particle and extended Kalman filtering when the state transition model is non-linear and the state transition and observation noise are correlated.
